title: kit.widgets-spec.v1
description: widgets.spec.json at a project root: who the project's interactive widgets are for (audiences), what they do (use cases), the stories they show (scenarios: actors, steps, inputs, expected outcomes), where the facts come from (sources: OpenAPI, JSON Schemas, engines, content), the project's vocabulary, tone, locales, brand theme and honesty labels, which widget archetypes apply and, for every widget, its usage (where and how it is used), application (the product surface it demonstrates), architecture (the components and flow it visualises, with the project's diagram) and utility (what the visitor learns and does). `kit widgets build` turns it into widgets.generated.json; widgets carry no content of their own (docs/WIDGETS.md).

project.description: The owning project: its key in the kit's project vocabulary registry (registry/vocabularies.json), its name and site.

repo.description: The project's repository: widgets link their architecture diagram there.

locales.description: Locales the widgets are generated in, the first is the default. dir and digits drive the runtime (RTL/LTR, numerals).

intl.description: Intl tag for dates and numbers (e.g. fa-IR, ar-SA-u-ca-islamic-umalqura, en-GB); default: the code.

tone.description: How the widgets speak: the register and the project's own writing notes (shown to authors, checked by review).

theme.description: Brand theme tokens: a module path (relative to the spec) whose default export holds the @saasreport/site tokens (color.accent, color.ink, …), or the token values inline. The runtime CSS is rendered from them.

honesty.description: Every widget says what its data is: live (read from a running service), engine (computed by the project's engine at build time), sample (illustrative). The labels are the project's words.

sources.description: The project's canonical sources (data contracts), by id. openapi, json-schema and content: a JSON file, a YAML file (with the project's yaml package) or a JS module (export: the named export, else the default) relative to the spec; engine: a module whose default export is an object of functions (call(args, { asOf, locale, addDays }) → JSON).

export.description: For a JS module source (openapi, json-schema, content): the named export holding the document (default: the default export). The project's canonical module is used as is, no JSON copy.

vocabulary.description: The project's own words: terms it owns (registered for the cross-project check), a glossary, and words its widgets must never use.

archetypes.description: The archetypes that apply to this project (a widget of another archetype fails the check).

asOf.description: The date engine calls and relative dates are computed from (deterministic builds; move it to refresh).

out.description: Where widgets.generated.json is written (relative to the spec).

page.description: The page that shows every widget (an @saasreport/site page of type widgets reads it).

exports.description: Projections of a feed widget into another kit consumer's shape (terminal-notify: the terminal's notify view).

as.description: An export kind that a registered archetype produces (its `exports`); build checks that one does.

includes.description: Spec parts merged into this spec before it is checked (paths relative to the spec): generated scenario families (e.g. one widget per page, derived from the project's content by the project's own generator). Each part may add sources, audiences, useCases and scenarios; ids stay unique across the whole spec. The parts are inputs of the build (their hashes are in widgets.generated.json).

plugins.description: The project's own archetype plugins (kit.widgets-plugin.v1): files, or folders with a plugin.mjs. Their ids start with the project's prefix.

archetype.description: The id of a registered archetype plugin (the kit's, or one the project declares in `plugins`); the registry says which exist.

text.description: A string in the default locale, a {locale: string} map, or a value taken from a source: {"$ref": "<source>#/json/pointer"} or {"$engine": {source, call, args}}.

at.description: When: an ISO date, a day offset from build.asOf ("+3d", "-1d"), or a sourced value.

operation.description: <openapi source>#<operationId>, or <openapi source>#<METHOD> <path> for documents without operationIds

payload.description: The response the playground shows instead of the OpenAPI sample: a value from a source or an engine call (e.g. the engine's real answer at build.asOf).

by.description: The actor who acts (approve by the initiator is refused).

chip.description: A short label for the step (a filter chip, a tab).

fails.description: A channel that fails in this story (the route falls back).

request.description: Request values the step sends (query parameters, body) instead of the OpenAPI examples.

device.description: The device this step's notification arrives on (archetype notify).

initiator.description: The actor who initiated the request: an approve action by this actor is refused (maker is not checker).

scene.description: What opens when the notification is tapped: an animated scene.

expr.description: Arithmetic over input ids: + - * / ( ), min, max, round, floor, ceil, pow, abs, gte(a, b) and lte(a, b) (1 or 0).

bands.description: Labelled ranges of the computed value (calculator): the band with the highest min not above the value is shown.

id.description: A region id a tour callout can anchor to.

regions.description: Named regions of the screen a tour callout can anchor to (beyond the lines).

usage.description: Where and how the widget is used on the project's surfaces (the generated page, a landing section, the terminal, an embed, an app).

application.description: The product surface the widget demonstrates (a product, an API, a console) and where it lives.

architecture.description: What the widget visualises of the project's architecture: its components, the flow, and the project's diagram of it (a file under docs/diagrams/, checked to exist).

utility.description: What the visitor learns from the widget and what they can do with it.

tour.description: A guided tour (archetype tour): a checklist of tasks, each a run of this scenario's steps; a callout pins a step to a named region of one of the scenario's screens. No lead form: the only call to action is on the finish card.

devices.description: Where notifications arrive (archetype notify): device mockups, each held by an actor.

machines.description: State machines (archetype machine): grouped (a sector, a product), each with its states and transitions.

meta.description: Short facts shown with the machine (regulations it implements, licence).

cases.description: Cases a runs widget lets the visitor pick (archetype runs): each runs through the scenario's steps (the stages) to its verdict.

stops.description: The step id where the case is stopped (held or refused); absent when it passes every stage.

workbench.description: The workbench (archetype workbench): the project's sources, panes, commands and layouts. Resolved per locale and validated against @saasreport/workbench's kit.workbench.v1 by `kit widgets build`; texts are strings, {locale: text} maps, {$ref} or {$engine}.

plugin.network.description: A network: nodes with roles around a hub, configurations (the views the visitor switches between) with their edges, typed flows, live counters and an optional provider-failover event.

mark.description: URL of the hub's image (the project's mark).

hub.description: The node id of the hub (a node of class hub).

default.description: The configuration shown first (default: the first).

selector.description: How the visitor switches configuration: tabs or a select (default: tabs up to six, else a select).

class.description: Its role in the topology; the stylesheet colours it from the project's tokens.

direction.description: forward: from to to (default); reverse: to to from; both: both ways.

reroute.description: The provider the flow continues through.

nodes.description: The nodes of this view (not the hub).

edges.description: Explicit edges as [from, to] node ids; default: every node to the hub.

plugin.flow.description: What travels along the scenario's steps (its hops, in order): an amount, a status sequence, figures, and optionally the API request and response.

amount.description: The amount that travels (as the project writes it, currency included).

metrics.description: Figures shown beside the path (counted up when it runs).

statuses.description: The status sequence; each status holds from its step until the next one's.

cta.description: The label of the button that runs it (default: the interface word).

step.description: The id of the scenario step where this status begins.

plugin.split.description: One amount and the allocations it divides into.

weight.description: Its share of the amount (any positive number); default: the number in its value.

plugin.netting.description: The participants, and the gross and net totals they collapse between.

count.description: The participant count as the project states it (shown beside the totals).

plugin.match.description: The two sides, their counts, and what to show when an exception is opened.

sample.description: How many records each side shows (default 8).

plugin.builder.description: The hub, the steps with their options, and the figures that count the selection.

class.description: The role the chosen options take in the preview.

step.description: Counts the options chosen in this step (default: in every step).
